title: Status rollup: a computed indicator of what a parent issue's children are doing

body.problem: Issue.parentId builds a real sub-issue hierarchy (134 issues imported from the OAPIL/SLG WBS) but nothing tells a reader what the children of a parent issue are doing without opening each one. In production one parent (OAPIL-091, In Progress) has its only child already closed.

source.reference: docs/plans/2026-09-02-status-rollup-design.md; live production data checked 2026-09-02 (29 parent issues)

scope_in: A computed statusRollup value per issue with children: Blocked if any leaf is blocked, In Progress if any leaf is active, Closed if every leaf is terminal, null for structural nodes and leaves
Recursive over descendants, so a grandchild's Task status is read rather than a stale intermediate Deliverable status
Shown in the detail panel Schedule tab and as a default-visible TreeGrid column
scope_out: Propagating status between parent and child in either direction: Issue.status stays a person-attested fact
Storing the rollup: it is derived, never persisted

acceptance_criteria.given: a parent issue whose leaves are all in a terminal status
acceptance_criteria.then: the parent's statusRollup is Closed regardless of the parent's own status

acceptance_criteria.given: a parent with at least one leaf in a blocked status
an issue with no children, or a structural node
acceptance_criteria.then: statusRollup is null and nothing is rendered for it

acceptance_criteria.given: a Deliverable whose child Task is Closed while the Deliverable itself is Open
acceptance_criteria.then: the grandparent's rollup reads Closed, proving recursion over leaves not direct children

business_rules: Derived values are never stored as fact: the rollup is computed in buildTree() and never written
TERMINAL_STATUSES and BLOCKED_STATUSES in lib/schedule.ts are the single source for the status families
